research_notes: Durapower Holdings is a Singapore-headquartered lithium-ion battery maker (founded 2009; HQ at 10 Kallang Sector, The EGIS, Singapore 349280). However, its actual battery CELL manufacturing is located in Suzhou, China, not Singapore. The existing Suzhou plant plus a new Suzhou factory (broke ground 2024, ~2.0 GWh/yr at full capacity, targeted operational Q2 2025) constitute its cell production; Singapore is HQ and R&D. Durapower's other sites are pack/assembly (DP NEXT in Thailand) or announced JVs (Poland ~2 GWh with Pozbud/Elmodis; Turkey with Kivanc Enerji; exploratory US facility, April 2025). No evidence of any battery cell manufacturing plant physically located in Singapore. Therefore is_cell_manufacturer set false for a 'Durapower Singapore' site — this candidate appears to be the corporate HQ rather than a distinct cell factory, and likely should not be a separate cell-manufacturing row. Status left null (no Singapore cell facility to assign a status to). Chemistry noted as NMC based on Durapower's Li-ion NMC product line, but this reflects the company generally, not a Singapore plant. Capacity/coordinates left null as no Singapore cell plant is sourced.

G-Cell semi-solid battery CELL plant in Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate, Rayong Province, Thailand — billed as ASEAN's first SemiSolid battery producer. Started operations 19 July 2021. Uses 24M Technologies (US) SemiSolid manufacturing technology under licence, producing LFP cells. Confirmed initial nameplate 30 MWh/year (0.03 GWh/yr), expandable to 100 MWh/year (0.1 GWh/yr); a 1 GWh facility was reported only as "under study" so not treated as firm nameplate. nameplate_capacity_gwh set to 0.1 GWh (the confirmed maximum of the current site); capacity_by_year_json shows 2021 initial 0.03 -> 2024 up-to-0.1. End market: ESS plus small EVs (tuk-tuks, buses, delivery motorcycles) — recorded as mixed. Cell format not clearly stated in sources (24M SemiSolid cells), left null. Operator/ownership: originally GPSC, then held by Nuovo Plus (JV Arun Plus 51% / GPSC 49%, both PTT Group). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: in 2024 Nuovo Plus signed a business transfer agreement selling the 30 MWh/yr plant, R&D centre and machinery to 24M Technologies (Nuovo Plus reinvesting ~USD 51m as a 24M shareholder), so as of late 2024 the physical site is owned/operated by 24M Technologies, which reopened it as a pilot/R&D facility capable of up to 100 MWh of SemiSolid cells. This is a small pilot-scale (sub-0.1 GWh) cell plant, not a large gigafactory. Distinct from the separate NV Gotion (Nuovo Plus x Gotion Hi-tech) 2 GWh pack plant, also in Thailand. Sources: GPSC press releases; electrive.com (2024-09-07); Bangkok Post (2246555); MarkLines (314150). Coordinates not sourced to precision, left null. Confidence 0.7: capacity/status well sourced but ownership has shifted and scale is small.

Samsung SDI's second battery cell plant at its Samsung SDI Energy Malaysia (SDIEM) complex in Seremban (Senawang), Negeri Sembilan. KRW 1.7 trillion / ~USD 1.3bn (RM5.8bn) investment announced July 2022, groundbreaking July 2022. Produces PRiMX 21700 cylindrical Li-ion cells (21mm x 70mm), nickel-based chemistry; end uses span EVs, power tools and micro-mobility (mixed). Mass production of 21700 cells targeted to begin 2024 with full plant completion in 2025 — treated as operational as of mid-2026. Capacity was NOT officially disclosed by Samsung SDI; market/industry estimates cited by ETNews/KED Global put it at ~15-20 GWh/yr, so nameplate figure (20 GWh, ref year 2025 at full ramp) is an estimate with reduced confidence. Samsung SDI has also flagged possible future 4680-format production at Seremban, not part of this Plant 2 scope. Coordinates left null (no precise sourced value). One physical site, wholly Samsung SDI owned (not a JV). Sources: electrive.com (2022-07-21), KED Global (ked202207210012), ETNews (2022-07-24), Korea Times (2024-09), The Edge Malaysia, paultan.org.

Located at Filinvest Innovation Park, New Clark City, Tarlac, Philippines. Australia–China JV between StB Capital Partners (Trevor St Baker's fund) and Oli Power; total project cost ~PHP 7bn. Inaugurated by President Marcos on 30 September 2024; construction began July 2023.

CELL MANUFACTURER = FALSE. Multiple sources, including the company's own overview, describe the site as assembling LFP battery modules and complete storage products (residential, C&I and utility-scale BESS, plus some EV packs) rather than manufacturing cells from raw electrode materials. LFP cells are almost certainly imported from the Chinese JV partner (Oli Power). Marketed as the Philippines' "first LFP battery gigafactory", but the process is module/pack assembly, so it falls outside the cell-manufacturing scope. Chemistry (LFP) is well sourced.

Capacity: initial line 300 MWh/yr (0.3 GWh/yr) as of 2024 — recorded as nameplate. A 2 GWh/yr-by-2030 target is widely cited but ambiguous: some sources (Reneweconomy) frame it as scaling this factory, while others (Philstar, Nov 2024) say it requires two additional factories in the Clark area — so 2 GWh is not confirmed as this single site's nameplate and is not recorded as such. ~70% of output is earmarked for export (Australia, Southeast Asia, North America), 30% domestic.

Coordinates left null: general location (New Clark City, Tarlac) is known but exact factory coordinates were not confirmed by a source. Cell format not stated.

VFlowTech is a Singapore-based manufacturer of vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB), marketed as "PowerCube" systems (250kWh units). It operates a manufacturing workshop in Tuas, Singapore. A US$10M Series A round (Feb 2023) funded a manufacturing facility with 200 MWh/year (0.2 GWh/year) annual production capacity for its VRFB PowerCubes — this is the capacity attributed to the Singapore/Tuas operation. The company manufactures its own VRFB stacks/cells in-house (true cell/stack manufacturing, not just pack assembly), so is_cell_manufacturer=true. cell_format left null as prismatic/cylindrical/pouch do not apply to flow-battery stacks. End market is grid/behind-the-meter ESS. Status set to operational because the Tuas workshop is described as an active manufacturing site, though the exact commissioning date is not explicitly confirmed — hence moderate confidence. Note: VFlowTech's larger "gigafactory" ambitions and a separate ~100 MWh facility are in India, not Singapore; those should not be conflated with this Tuas site. No specific facility coordinates could be sourced (Tuas is a district). Primary source: Energy-Storage.News (single reputable tracker); Tuas location also referenced in search snippets and Singapore EMA/JTC feature stories (returned 403 on direct fetch).

Announced April 2021 as an 8 GWh lithium-ion battery cell gigafactory ("gigafab") to be built on a greenfield site at Nong Yai, Chonburi province, as a JV with Rojana Industrial Park Public Co. Ltd (Rojana 55% / EVLOMO 45%, up to ~$1.06bn investment). Planned phase 1 of 1 GWh (~$143m) over 18-24 months, scaling to 8 GWh; output intended for 2- and 4-wheelers, buses, heavy vehicles and ESS (hence end_market=mixed). CRITICAL STATUS NOTE: This specific Nong Yai site never proceeded. Around Sept 2021 EVLOMO and Rojana "parted ways" and EVLOMO relocated the project to CPGC Industrial Estate in Rayong (a different physical site). No evidence the Nong Yai plant was ever built or moved beyond the terminated MoU, so it should be treated as an abandoned announcement rather than an active project — hence low confidence. Chemistry described only as generic "lithium"/lithium-ion; cell format and exact ramp years not disclosed. No exact site coordinates found (Nong Yai district, Chonburi), so lat/long left null. Note separately: EVLOMO's later 2023 Schneider Electric tie-up was a 1 GW battery PACK plant, not cell manufacturing. Sources: PR Newswire (parted-ways release, Sept 2021); pv-magazine 2021-05-06; Green Car Congress 2021-04-24; electrive 2021-04-26.

Gigafactory Malaysia Sdn Bhd is a wholly-owned subsidiary of NanoMalaysia Berhad (a company under Malaysia's Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, MOSTI). The facility is a 1,500 sq m plant in Suria Industrial Park, Sepang, Selangor, Malaysia. It manufactures a homegrown graphene-enhanced NMC lithium-ion battery CELL, developed at a cost of RM20 million. Small-scale commercial cell production was scheduled to begin July 2026, ramping to maximum capacity of 1 MWh/year (= 92,000 cells/year) as early as September 2026. NOTE: nameplate is only ~1 MWh/year = 0.001 GWh/year — this is effectively a pilot/small-scale commercial line, NOT a true multi-GWh gigafactory despite the "Gigafactory" branding. End market is EV; company also eyeing ESS/export markets (Indonesia, South Korea, India, Pakistan) and a nickel-supply partnership with Indonesia. Reported as the first homegrown battery cell manufacturing in ASEAN. Status marked operational as commercial production was launching in July 2026 (research date 2026-07-18), but this is a very fresh launch — could be treated as under_construction/ramping; hence moderate confidence. Coordinates left null (exact site coordinates not confirmed by a source). Cell format not disclosed in sources. Multiple reputable outlets (The Edge Malaysia, Yahoo Finance/Just Auto, SoyaCincau, paultan.org, battery-tech.net) corroborate location, capacity, chemistry and timeline.

Panasonic Energy operates its own cell-manufacturing lines (14 lines, adding a 15th) inside Tesla's Gigafactory Nevada building in Storey County, near Sparks/Reno, NV. Cells are 2170-format cylindrical Li-ion with NCA chemistry, supplied to Tesla for Model 3/Model Y (EV end market). Mass cell production began Jan 2017; site announced 2014. Panasonic's cell capacity is variously reported at ~38-41 GWh/year, with a ~10% expansion (new 2170 line, ~1-2 yr build) taking it toward ~41-42 GWh; sources conflict (some cite 38->39, others 41), so nameplate set to 41 GWh (2025 ref) with moderate confidence. Not a legal cell JV: Panasonic owns/operates its cell lines while Tesla owns the building and co-developed the site; single physical site, one row, Tesla listed as partner. Separately, Tesla runs its own 4680 cell/pack lines at the same complex (not counted here). Coordinates are the commonly documented location of the Gigafactory Nevada complex. source_date reflects access date; underlying reporting spans 2017-2023. Additional sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigafactory_Nevada, pv-magazine.com/2017/01/04/teslapanasonic-begin-battery-cell-production-at-nevada-gigafactory/, automotivemanufacturingsolutions.com.

In-house Tesla 4680 cylindrical cell plant co-located at Gigafactory Texas (unincorporated Travis County, near Austin), supplying Cybertruck and Model Y. Wholly owned by Tesla, not a JV. Cell production ramped from ~2022/early 2023; Tesla reported passing 20M cells (Oct 2023) and 50M cells (Dec 2024). Confirmed operational. 4680 uses a high-nickel cathode (NCA/NCM-type), dry-electrode process (both anode and cathode dry-coated as of Q4 2025 earnings call, 28 Jan 2026). CAPACITY IS UNCERTAIN and mixes actual vs target: reputable reporting put the actual run rate at ~6.2 GWh/yr in early 2024 (used in capacity_by_year_json as a rough ramp, 2023-2024). Tesla's stated eventual goal is ~100 GWh/yr (reported plan of 20-25 GWh per line, expanding toward 8 lines) - recorded here as nameplate_capacity_gwh (target, not yet built/verified). One web-search summary cited a 40 GWh installed figure attributed to an SEC 8-K, but I could not confirm this in a primary source and treat it as unverified. Coordinates ~30.2222, -97.6171 (site centroid). Lower confidence overall because current vs nameplate capacity figures are inconsistent across sources and the 100 GWh figure is aspirational.

Panasonic Energy's second US battery cell plant, located at Astra Enterprise Park (former Sunflower Army Ammunition Plant site), De Soto, Kansas, ~300 acres / 4.7m sq ft. Wholly owned by Panasonic Energy (parent: Panasonic Holdings); not a JV. Announced July 2022, groundbreaking 2 Nov 2022 (~$4bn investment, ~4,000 direct jobs). Grand opening 14 July 2025, when Panasonic Energy began mass production of 2170 cylindrical Li-ion cells (NCA chemistry, consistent with Panasonic's Tesla-supplied 2170 cells; chemistry inferred, not explicitly stated in release). Full nameplate target ~32 GWh/yr; ramp to full capacity is phased and has been delayed beyond the original ~2027 timeline, so capacity_ref_year left null and no sourced year-by-year ramp available. Primary customer is Tesla; end market EV. In June 2026 Panasonic announced (~$2.18bn) plans to convert part of the De Soto plant to produce cells for data-center/ESS applications from Q3 2029, so end market is shifting toward mixed but is currently EV. Coordinates not confirmed from a primary source, left null.

chemistry: mixed (NMC for EV, LFP for ESS)
research_notes: Wholly owned LG Energy Solution site in Holland, Michigan (LG Energy Solution Michigan, Inc.) — not a JV. Original plant (former LG Chem Michigan) began EV battery cell production in 2013 producing NMC pouch cells (~5 GWh). In March 2022 LGES announced a $1.7bn (later cited ~$1.4bn) expansion. On 24 June 2025 LGES opened newly converted LFP cell lines for grid-scale energy storage (ESS) — the first large-scale LFP battery cell production in the US — with LFP production having started in May 2025. Reported ESS LFP capacity: 16.5 GWh at the new lines, scaling to 17 GWh by end-2025 and 30 GWh by end-2026 (per Q2 2025 earnings call, reported by Solar Power World, July 2025). Combined with ~5 GWh legacy EV capacity this gives a full-site nameplate of roughly 35 GWh/yr by 2026 (mixed EV + ESS). nameplate_capacity_gwh (35) and capacity_by_year_json (2025:22 = 5 EV + 17 ESS; 2026:35 = 5 EV + 30 ESS) combine EV and ESS lines and carry some uncertainty because EV-line utilisation amid cooling EV demand is unclear; the clearly sourced figure is the ESS LFP ramp to 30 GWh by end-2026. Cell format: legacy EV cells are pouch; LFP ESS cell format not definitively confirmed (hence 'mixed'). Coordinates left null (site ~West Shore Drive/A-32 area of Holland, MI; exact figures not confirmed by source). Sources: LG Energy Solution newsroom (news.lgensol.com/company-news/supplementary-stories/681/); Solar Power World 'LGES to expand Michigan ESS battery plant to 30 GWh' (July 2025); Canary Media and CleanTechnica (June 2025) on the LFP plant opening (1.7M sq ft, ~1,700 jobs).

chemistry: mixed (46-series/4680 cylindrical NCM for EV; LFP for ESS)
research_notes: Single ~$5.5bn stand-alone battery complex in Queen Creek, Arizona, announced March 2023. Wholly owned by LG Energy Solution (not a JV). Two cell-manufacturing lines on one site: (1) a cylindrical EV-battery plant making 46-series (4680) cells, ~36 GWh/yr, and (2) an LFP pouch ESS-battery plant, ~17 GWh/yr — combined full nameplate ~53 GWh/yr. nameplate_capacity_gwh=53 is the eventual full-complex figure; the active cylindrical line alone is ~36 GWh. The LFP/ESS line was paused in June 2024 (not cancelled) as LGES adjusts investment pace. As of 2025 the cylindrical plant was ~50–60% complete with sample/mass production of 46-series cells targeted for mid-to-late 2026; the site is best classed under_construction (not yet operational as of mid-2026). Cylindrical line originally planned for 2170 cells (~27 GWh) before the shift to 46-series (~36 GWh). Coordinates left null — precise plant coordinates not sourced (site is in the northeastern area of Queen Creek, AZ). Figures corroborated by KED Global, electrive, Manufacturing Dive, Queen Creek town releases and Arizona Commerce Authority.

First of the Ultium Cells plants (a GM–LG Energy Solution 50/50 JV). Groundbreaking May 2020; cell production began late August 2022. GM Q4 2023 earnings and GM Authority (Feb 2024) reported the plant reached full/100% capacity by end of Q4 2023; produced its 100 millionth cell by December 2024, confirming operational status. Nameplate capacity is widely reported as ~35 GWh/year (some sources cite a 40+ GWh target); used 35 GWh as the annual nameplate with 2024 as the reference year. Chemistry is GM's high-nickel NCMA (nickel-cobalt-manganese-aluminum) in a long-pouch format, supplying GM EVs (Cadillac Lyriq, GMC Hummer EV, Chevy Silverado EV). Address: 7400 Tod Ave SW, Lordstown/Warren, OH 44481 (the plant sits in the Lordstown area near GM's Lordstown complex; the city of Warren is used in Ultium's own naming). Coordinates are approximate to the confirmed Lordstown site (~41.16, -80.85) — not an exact surveyed point, so treat as town/site-level. No capacity ramp JSON available beyond confirmation that it ramped to full by late 2023. Sources: ultiumcell.com location page, gmauthority.com (Oct 2023 75% capacity; Feb 2024 full capacity; Dec 2024 100M cells), insideevs.com (production start).

Second Ultium Cells plant (JV of General Motors and LG Energy Solution), a single physical site at 301 Donald F. Ephlin Pkwy, Spring Hill, TN 37174, next to GM's Spring Hill Assembly. ~2.8M sq ft; ~$2.3bn investment announced 2021, plus a $275M expansion (Dec 2022) that raised planned capacity from 35 GWh to 50 GWh/yr. Cell production began Feb 2024, initially NMC pouch cells for GM EVs (Cadillac Lyriq/Vistiq). In July 2025 GM/LG announced converting some lines to LFP; ~$70M investment to begin LFP cells for ESS (via LG Energy Solution Vertech) around Q2 2026, with fuller LFP EV-cell commercial production expected by ~2027. So it is now a mixed NMC (EV) + LFP (ESS) site. Nameplate 50 GWh is the eventual full figure; it opened at ~35 GWh — year-by-year ramp timing not precisely sourced, so capacity_by_year_json is approximate. Coordinates left null (no sourced lat/long; site is adjacent to GM Spring Hill Assembly). Corroborating sources: TN.gov/TNECD (Dec 2022 $275M expansion), CNBC (2025-07-14), electrive (2025-07-15), gmauthority (2024 shipments; 2026 LFP start), KED Global.

plant_name: Ultium Cells Lansing (Factory 3, Delta Township, Michigan)
research_notes:
Third Ultium Cells plant, in Delta Township near Lansing, Michigan (~2.8m sq ft, $2.6bn). Announced Jan 2022 by the GM-LG Energy Solution JV (Ultium Cells LLC) with a stated ~50 GWh/yr full-production nameplate. In Dec 2024 GM agreed to sell its stake to LG Energy Solution; the deal closed in Q1 2025, so the site is now WHOLLY OWNED and operated by LG Energy Solution (no longer a JV — jv_partners left null; GM is the former JV partner). LG is repurposing the plant to build high-nickel NCMA pouch cells/modules for Toyota EVs assembled in the US.

STATUS: building is "nearing completion"; multiple mid-2026 reports state LG is targeting the START of mass production within 2026 (originally slated for late 2025). Since confirmed mass production had not yet begun as of the sources reviewed (mid-2026), recorded as under_construction rather than operational — this is the main uncertainty; it may already be ramping. start_year set to 2026 (target); could slip.

CAPACITY: sources conflict. Original 2022 JV announcement = 50 GWh/yr at full production (used as nameplate here). More recent trackers/press (2025-2026) cite ~40-41 GWh/yr for the plant as built ("will have an annual capacity of 41 GWh"; LG "planning to secure capacity of 40 GWh depending on demand"). No reliable phased ramp figures found, so capacity_by_year_json left null and capacity_ref_year null. Coordinates not sourced to a precise figure, left null (Delta Township, MI).

Note: this is DISTINCT from (a) LG's separate Holland, MI LFP-ESS plant, and (b) the separate ~$4.3bn Tesla-LG LFP prismatic plant planned in Lansing (production ~2027). Sources: LGES press release (news.lgensol.com/company-news/press-releases/881/); Utility Dive on GM stake sale (utilitydive.com/news/gm-sells-stake-ultium-cells-lg-energy-solution-ev-batttery-plant/734667/); TheElec on Toyota/40GWh (thelec.net idxno=5214); Center for American Progress plant profile.

parent_company: Ford Motor Company / SK On (joint venture)
research_notes: Two co-located battery cell plants ("Kentucky 1" and "Kentucky 2") on a single ~1,500-acre campus in Glendale, Hardin County, Kentucky; treated as one physical site. Each plant ~43 GWh/yr for a combined ~86 GWh/yr nameplate (some sources cite 37 + 45 GWh; the 43 + 43 = 86 GWh figure is most commonly cited). Kentucky 1 began commercial EV cell production 19 Aug 2025 (Ford F-150 Lightning, E-Transit); Kentucky 2 start delayed to ~2027 (Bloomberg/electrive), hence the phased ramp in capacity_by_year_json. Site status set to operational because plant 1 is producing. JV of Ford (BlueOval) and SK On, ~$5.8bn investment. Chemistry NMC; SK On produces pouch-format cells (cell_format inferred from SK On's standard pouch technology, high confidence but not explicitly stated for this site). Coordinates are approximate town-level for Glendale, KY (~37.60, -85.89) and not confirmed to exact plant footprint - treat as low-precision. announced_year 2021 reflects the Sept 2021 Ford/SK announcement; groundbreaking Dec 2022. Sources: kentucky.gov Gov. Beshear release (production begins Aug 2025); electrive.com (2025-08-20); koreaherald.com; insideevs.com; electriccarsreport.com (86 GWh, NMC, 2022 groundbreaking).

parent_company: LG Energy Solution / Honda Motor (joint venture)
research_notes: Cell manufacturing plant in Jefferson Township, Fayette County, near Jeffersonville, Ohio (~40 miles SW of Columbus). >2 million sq ft; ~$4.4bn total investment (initially $3.5bn); >1,000 employees. JV of LG Energy Solution and Honda Motor, announced Oct 2022, formal JV (L-H Battery Company) established 2023, groundbreaking Feb 2023. Originally designed for ~40 GWh/yr of pouch-type lithium-ion EV cells for Honda. After the Trump administration ended US BEV purchase incentives and Honda cancelled its North American BEV programme, the plant pivoted to ESS cell production (plus future HEV cells). Mass production of ESS lithium-ion cells began 1 July 2026 — hence status 'operational'. First cells are integrated into energy storage systems by LG Energy Solution Vertech for grid/utility, C&I and residential markets. Nameplate 40 GWh/yr is the original/eventual full capacity cited in July 2026 reporting; no phased ramp figures published, so capacity_by_year_json left null and 40 GWh treated as full nameplate. Chemistry not explicitly confirmed for the ESS pivot; recorded as NMC pouch, inferred from the plant's original LG EV pouch-cell design — treat chemistry as lower-confidence. In Dec 2025 Honda agreed to buy the building and related assets from LG for ~KRW4.22tn (~$2.85-2.9bn), expected to close ~28 Feb 2026, but the L-H Battery JV continues to operate the plant under a lease, so it is kept as a single JV site with both partners. Coordinates not confirmed from a source, left null. Sources: lhbattery.com press release (1 Jul 2026); energy-storage.news (3 Jul 2026); Korea Times / Seoul Economic Daily (3 Jul 2026); Utility Dive / WardsAuto (Dec 2025 sale); Honda/LGES JV releases (2022-2023).

Battery cell plant at BlueOval City, Haywood County near Stanton, TN; ~$5.6bn site. Originally the Ford/SK On 50:50 JV "BlueOval SK". In Dec 2025 Ford and SK On agreed to dissolve the JV: a Ford subsidiary takes the two Kentucky plants and SK On takes full ownership and operation of the single Tennessee plant (deal subject to regulatory approval, expected complete ~Q1 2026), hence operator = SK On solo and jv_partners left null. Nameplate ~43 GWh/yr (some earlier DOE/environmental documents cite 45 GWh; original BlueOval City figure 43 GWh). Chemistry NMC (nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode, graphite anode). As of early 2026 construction is essentially complete but the plant is NOT yet producing — commissioning/pre-production stage — so classed under_construction rather than operational. Production timeline repeatedly slipped: from 2025 to 2026/2027, and after the split SK On slated battery production for 2028 (start_year=2028). End market originally EV cells for Ford BEVs; after Ford scaled back EV plans, SK On plans to supply Ford under a supply agreement AND other customers including stationary energy storage (ESS), so end_market marked mixed. ~300 employed in TN as of late 2025; ~150 laid off March 2026. Coordinates left null (no hard-sourced lat/long; site is roughly Stanton/Haywood County, TN). Cross-checked: Wikipedia (BlueOval SK), Tennessee Lookout, Utility Dive, Ford Authority, Korea Herald, DOE environmental assessment.

Two lithium-ion cell plants on one physical campus at 1760 SK Boulevard, Commerce, GA (Jackson County), operated by SK Battery America, a wholly owned SK On subsidiary (not a JV). Plant 1 (~9.8 GWh) began production early 2022; Plant 2 (~11.7 GWh) came online 2023, for a combined ~21.5 GWh/yr (some sources round to 22 GWh). ~$2.6bn invested; ~3,000+ employees. Chemistry is NCM/NMC pouch cells supplying Ford F-150 Lightning and VW ID.4; SK On is converting some lines to LFP and has signed US ESS supply deals, so end market is shifting from pure EV toward mixed EV/ESS. Coordinates are approximate (Commerce, GA city level); precise plant pin not independently confirmed. Capacity/status cross-checked across InsideEVs, SK newsroom, Georgia.gov and trade press.

plant_name: Samsung SDI-GM Battery Plant (New Carlisle, Indiana)
research_notes: $3.5bn JV between GM and Samsung SDI in New Carlisle, Indiana (680-acre site, ~1,600 jobs). Announced June 2023; JV finalised 28 Aug 2024. Manufactures nickel-rich prismatic NCA cells for EVs. Initial nameplate 27 GWh/yr, expandable to 36 GWh/yr (nameplate figure used = 36 GWh; ~300,000 EVs). Cell production originally targeted 2026, pushed to 2027. In May 2026 GM and Samsung SDI PAUSED construction to align capacity with lower EV demand (Barton Malow contractor layoffs reported), so 2027 start is now uncertain. Classified under_construction because the site is physically built out (steel superstructure went vertical) but not operational; status is a paused construction project, not merely announced. Coordinates are approximate for New Carlisle town (~41.70, -86.51); exact plant-site coordinates not confirmed from a source, so lat/long confidence is low. capacity_by_year_json left null as no sourced year-by-year ramp available. Other sources: insideevs.com/news/731721, wardsauto.com finalize-joint-venture, gmauthority.com 2026/05 pause, sbrchamber.com GM project FAQs.

StarPlus Energy is the 50:50 JV between Stellantis and Samsung SDI. The Kokomo campus consists of two adjacent lithium-ion battery cell (and module) plants treated here as one physical site. Plant 1: ~33 GWh/yr, targeted to begin production Q1 2025. Plant 2: ~34 GWh/yr, targeted for early 2027. Combined nameplate ~67 GWh/yr at full build (ref 2027), enough for ~670,000 vehicles/yr. Total investment >$6.3bn; a $7.54bn DOE Loan Programs Office loan closed Dec 2024. Chemistry is Samsung SDI NMC prismatic cells (PRiMX); cell_format prismatic inferred from Samsung SDI's product line. Status set to under_construction for the overall site because plant 2 is still being built; plant 1 was slated to start production in 2025 (start_year 2025) but no independent confirmation of actual first-cell production was found — if plant 1 is confirmed running, the site status would be partially operational. Coordinates left null (specific site coordinates not sourced; site is adjacent to existing Stellantis operations in Kokomo, IN). A possible third plant has been discussed but is not firmly scheduled and is excluded. Capacity figures corroborated by Stellantis press releases, Greater Kokomo, Manufacturing Dive and DOE. Sources: Stellantis press release (2023-10-11); DOE StarPlus / EA-2263 pages; Manufacturing Dive on the $7.5bn DOE loan (Dec 2024).

jv_partners: Toyota Motor North America, Toyota Tsusho
research_notes: Site at the Greensboro-Randolph Megasite in Liberty, Randolph County, North Carolina. Announced 6 Dec 2021 (initial ~$1.29bn); investment scaled up in multiple stages to ~$13.9bn, with a further $10bn pledged over five years. Production began in 2025 (plant opening event 12 Nov 2025); it is Toyota's first battery plant outside Japan and its 11th US plant. Confirmed to be a genuine CELL manufacturer, not just pack/module assembly: multiple sources describe a vertically integrated operation covering cathode/anode electrode processing, cell assembly, formation, and module assembly under one roof. 14 production lines (10 for BEV/PHEV, 4 for HEV) supporting HEV, PHEV and BEV modules; nameplate ~30 GWh/year at full capacity, targeted around 2030 (enough for ~400,000 70 kWh BEVs). Initial output focuses on HEV modules shipped to Toyota Kentucky and Mazda Toyota Manufacturing Alabama. Chemistry recorded as lithium-ion (specific cathode chemistry not disclosed in sources); cell format not confirmed, left null. Exact coordinates not confirmed by a source, left null. TBMNC is a Toyota-group entity (Toyota Motor North America with Toyota Tsusho); treated as one operator with those listed as partners, not double-counted. Corroborating sources: Toyota USA Newsroom facility page, batterytechonline, Automotive Logistics, InsideEVs, Electrek.

AESC (formerly Envision AESC) gigafactory at the Kentucky Transpark, Bowling Green, Warren County, Kentucky. Announced April 2022 as a $2bn, 30 GWh cell-and-module plant to power up to ~300,000 EVs/year; 1.6m sq ft; ~2,000 jobs. Broke ground 2022, structural completion Sept 2023. Cells manufactured on-site (not just pack assembly), so is_cell_manufacturer=true. Original plan: some functions in 2025, full operation by 2027. As of mid-2025 the plant was still under construction; a June 2025 Wall Street Journal report of a halt was denied by AESC and local officials, who confirmed Bowling Green construction continued toward a 2027 operational date (the paused site was AESC's separate Florence, South Carolina BMW plant). Company has signalled a pivot to include energy storage (ESS) alongside EV cells, hence end_market=mixed. Single physical site in Florence County's Florence Global Technology & Commerce Park (off East Old Marion Highway, near Wilson High School), ~1.5M sq ft. AESC (majority owned by China's Envision Group) is building the plant to supply BMW's US EV operations (Spartanburg / Neue Klasse) with 46120 large-format cylindrical cells; cathode is nickel-rich, anode silicon-doped. Nameplate widely cited at 30 GWh/yr; initial ~$810m investment announced Dec 2022, groundbreaking June 2023, plus subsequent expansions (Dec 2023, Mar 2024) raising total planned investment to ~$1.6bn. Construction was PAUSED in June 2025 (after ~$1.2bn invested, site ~75% complete) citing US EV/tariff/policy uncertainty; as of mid-2026 the project remains paused but active with restart discussions ongoing and production still nominally targeted for 2026 (timeline under pressure).
